paragraphs.text: Non nisi dimenso prius montis ambitu. The prophet saw not the glory of God till he had first seen the mount measured, the temple restored. Men must usually wait upon God in the use of means ere they see the King in his glory.
paragraphs.anchor: Afterwards he brought me.

paragraphs.text: Men must awake out of the west of wickedness, and stand up from dead courses and companies, if Christ, the Day Star from on high, shall give them light. {Eph 5:14 Luk 1:78-79}
paragraphs.anchor: Even the gate that looketh toward the east.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The vision of the glory. God, who by the east gate had left the temple and the city, {Eze 10:19} doth now the same way return, and filleth the house with the glory of his presence.
paragraphs.anchor: And behold the glory

paragraphs.text: Importing the multitude of his attendants, and his irresistible power, in his gospel especially, which is the power of God to salvation, and, like a mighty torrent, bears down all before it.
paragraphs.anchor: And his voice was like a noise of many waters.

paragraphs.text: How can it do otherwise when the Sun of righteousness cometh in place, and irradiateth both organ and object. {2Co 4:6} Into Solomon’s temple God came in a thick cloud; not so here. Light is now more diffused than ever. Woe be to those that wink, or who seek straws to put out their eyes with, as Bernard hath it.
paragraphs.anchor: And the earth shined with his glory.

paragraphs.text: Being so much the sweeter and the welcomer to me. Hence he so oft repeateth it; and the Jewish doctors observe that eight times in this one verse, visionis ac videndi vocabulum repetitur, the word for vision and to see it is made use of.
paragraphs.anchor: And it was according to the vision.

paragraphs.text: i.e., To foretell the destruction of it, {Eze 9:2; Eze 9:5} from which time forth it was a done thing. See Jer 1:10. {See Trapp on "Jer 1:10"}
paragraphs.anchor: When I came to destroy the city

paragraphs.text: In reverence to his majesty, in admiration of his mercy, and in the sense of mine own unworthiness. The nearer any one cometh to God, the lower he falleth in his own eyes, and the more doth "rottenness enter into his bones."
paragraphs.anchor: And I fell upon my face.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 43:2.
paragraphs.anchor: And the glory of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: The ordinary entrance into the temple. There, if anywhere, God is to be found. Where should a man be sought for but at his house? Say he be from home a while, yet thither he returneth; so here.
paragraphs.anchor: By the way of the gate.

paragraphs.text: Who was fallen upon my face. The lowly shall be lifted up.
paragraphs.anchor: So the spirit took me up.

paragraphs.text: As being a priest. So is every true believer. {1Pe 2:9 Rev 1:6}
paragraphs.anchor: And brought me into the inner court.

paragraphs.text: God’s presence is the full glory of each good soul. See Hag 2:7.
paragraphs.anchor: Filled the house.

paragraphs.text: The man Christ Jesus, standing by. Here, then, is a meeting and the mystery of the blessed Trinity; yea, here is a double mystery to be taken notice of, viz., those two wonderful unions of three persons in one God, and of Christ’s two natures in one person.
paragraphs.anchor: And I heard him speaking unto me.

paragraphs.text: i.e., My Church, which is unto me instead of heaven and earth. Behold the place of my throne, &c., {Isa 60:1} so some read it; others, As for the place of my throne, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: The place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet

paragraphs.text: But hallow; for negative holiness alone is little worth.
paragraphs.anchor: No more defile.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Their idols; {a} not unfitly called "carcases": - (1.) Because void of life; (2.) Stinking stuff. See Lev 26:30 Jer 16:18. These were oft brought in, and countenanced by their kings.
paragraphs.anchor: Nor by the carcases of their kings

paragraphs.text: {a} Piscat.

By broaching falsehoods for truth, and setting human devices in competition with the good Word of God. That detestable decree of the Council of Trent is well known, whereby the Apocrypha is set cheek by jowl, as they say, with the holy canon; the Vulgate translation with the original; traditions with Scriptures, and unwritten verities with those that are written. This is intolerable presumption. Jews and Turks do the like in their Talmud and Koran; that I speak not of our sect masters, who boldly obtrude their placits without just reproof, and require to be believed.
paragraphs.anchor: In their setting of their threshold by my thresholds.

paragraphs.text: Which they have wretchedly set up by their sins, to their singular disadvantage; {Isa 59:2} or, They have come under my nose, as it were, to provoke me; or, The nearer they were to Church, the farther from God.
paragraphs.anchor: And the wall between me and them.

paragraphs.text: So shall all be well between us. See Jer 3:1 Isa 1:18. {See Trapp on "Jer 3:1"} {See Trapp on "Isa 1:18"} Piscator; Ictus sapiat. Some read it, Now they will put away, &c.; and so they did, after the captivity, but will not be yet drawn to worship the true God aright. The Lord persuade their hearts thereto. Fiat, Fiat! Do it, Do it!
paragraphs.anchor: Now let them put away their whoredom.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 43:7.
paragraphs.anchor: And the carcases.

paragraphs.text: This is the same with that in Mat 28:20, "I am with you to the end of the world."
paragraphs.anchor: And I will dwell in the midst of them for ever.

paragraphs.text: Heb., That house - sc., Which I have showed thee in visions; the idea of that temple which shall shortly be set up, its figure and dimensions.
paragraphs.anchor: Show the house.

paragraphs.text: Of having dealt so unworthily with a God so gracious.
paragraphs.anchor: That they may be ashamed.

paragraphs.text: Ut metiantur universe; that, by a holy geometry, they may, in the spirit of their minds, take all the dimensions of it, and be transformed into the likeness of the heavenly pattern. These are those holy and heavenly mathematics, which none can learn but those that are taught of God, and without which none can be Christ’s disciple; like as none might be scholar to Plato that had not the grounds of geometry. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And let them measure the pattern.

paragraphs.text: {a} Scholae Platonis haec fuit inscriptio, ουδεις αγεωμετρητος εισιτω.

If they blush and bleed at heart for their iniquities. Penitents are to be taught the truth which is according to godliness, and all such are exactly to know and to do the whole will of God, as had not rather be carnally secured than soundly comforted.
paragraphs.anchor: And if they be ashamed of all that they have done.

paragraphs.text: The Church is as a city on a hill, seen far and near, {Mat 5:14} and the members of it are still ascending from one degree of grace to another, from strength to strength, till they see the face of God in Zion. {Psa 15:1 Heb 12:22-23}
paragraphs.anchor: Upon the top of the mountain.

paragraphs.text: All the Lord’s people are so, at least in profession, first steps, honest endeavour, divine acceptation, and shall be so one day in all perfection. {Rev 21:8; Rev 21:27; Rev 22:14-15}
paragraphs.anchor: The whole limit thereof round about shall be most holy.

paragraphs.text: viz., Of burnt offerings, which was in the priests’ court, and not at all spoken of till now.
paragraphs.anchor: And these are the measures of the altar

paragraphs.text: viz., That of the sanctuary.
paragraphs.anchor: The cubit

paragraphs.text: Heb., The bosom.
paragraphs.anchor: Even the bottom.

paragraphs.text: Heb., The back, as that which bore all. "We have also an altar," {Heb 13:10} even Jesus Christ, the just one, who is both our Ariel (God’s lion, Rev 5:5) and our Hareel (God’s mount) of four cubits, as being "preached unto the Gentiles" in all parts, "believed on in the world, received up into glory." {1Ti 3:16}
paragraphs.anchor: This shall be the higher place.

paragraphs.text: This so exact measuring of the altar may import, saith Polanus, the faithful and perfect preaching of the gospel by the apostles, and all faithful ministers of God’s word after them. {2Co 10:13-18 1Co 4:1,2Ki 11:1}
paragraphs.anchor: And from the bottom upon the ground.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Hareel, the hill of God, or the only place of sacrifices.
paragraphs.anchor: So the altar.

paragraphs.text: Ariel, the lion of God; so called because the fire of this altar devoured the sacrifices, as a lion doth the prey. See Isa 29:16.
paragraphs.anchor: And from the altar.

paragraphs.text: Christ, the Christian altar, is complete, firm, and fixed.
paragraphs.anchor: Square in the four squares thereof.

paragraphs.text: As leading to the Sun of righteousness, and the light of eternal blessedness, arising out of heaven.
paragraphs.anchor: And his stairs shall look toward the east.

paragraphs.text: Christians also have their sacrifices, though of another alloy, to offer, and must look to the ordinances of their altar; ministers must especially.
paragraphs.anchor: These are the ordinances of the altar.

paragraphs.text: All this is to be understood spiritually, as being figuratively spoken.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt give to the priests.

paragraphs.text: Together with a goat and a ram. {Eze 43:22-23; Eze 43:25} All that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh, with the affections and lusts, {Gal 5:24} and are still doing at it.
paragraphs.anchor: A young bullock.

paragraphs.text: Christ, as mediator, was consecrated and qualified for the work.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt take of the blood.

paragraphs.text: So Christ suffered without the gate. {Heb 13:11-12}
paragraphs.anchor: Ver. 2l. Without the sanctuary.

paragraphs.text: To set forth how Christ cleanseth and sanctifieth his people. {Heb 9:19-24 Joh 17:19 Heb 9:13-14}
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall cleanse the altar.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 43:19.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt offer.

paragraphs.text: Christians must "have salt {a} within themselves," {Mar 9:50} and see to it that all their speeches be seasoned with the salt of mortification and discretion; {Eph 4:29 Col 4:6} so shall God make an everlasting covenant with them, even a "covenant of salt." See Lev 2:13.
paragraphs.anchor: And the priests shall cast salt upon them.

paragraphs.text: {a} Plato sal nominat Yεοφιλεστατον diis churis. Nihil utilius sale ac sole. - Coel. Rhodig., lib. vi. cap. 1.
Mortification must be a Christian’s daily practice.
paragraphs.anchor: Every day a goat.

paragraphs.text: Thou and they together. We must also sanctify the Lord God in our hearts. {1Pe 3:15}
paragraphs.anchor: They shall purge.

paragraphs.text: The services of mortified men shall be accepted, on the eighth day especially, the Christian Sabbath, in the holy assemblies.
paragraphs.anchor: It shall be upon the eighth day.
